name: Thrown-form alteration
summary: A potter throws a plain vessel on the wheel and then bends, pinches, cuts and joins it while it is wet, so that the vessel becomes an animal or a figure.
how: Throw a bottle, a vase or a jug on the wheel.
Close the neck, or pinch out ears and a beak.
Press the belly and add arms or legs of slip.
Draw the face with a knife or a brush.

origin.note: Picasso asks the throwers at the Madoura pottery for plain forms and turns them into owls, bulls and women.

adoptions.via: Picasso alters thrown vases at the Madoura pottery, and the editions copy his altered forms.
Voulkos and his students cut and tear thrown cylinders, and stack them into large forms.
